4.3.4.7 Memory Protection and Pointer Type Parameters in RTE API
In a memory protected ECU, a SW-C from an untrusted partition might misuse the transition to the trusted context to modify memory in another partition. This can occur when a pointer to a different memory partition is passed from the untrusted partition to the trusted context. The RTE shall avoid this misuse by at least checking the validity of the address of the pointer, and, where possible, also checking the integrity of the associated memory object.
[SWS_Rte_02752] ⌈When a SW-C in an untrusted partition receives (OUT parameter) or provides (IN parameter with composite data type) an ArgumentDataPrototype or VariableDataPrototype, it hands over a pointer to a memory object to an RTE API. The RTE shall only forward this pointer to a trusted SW-C after it has checked that the whole memory object is owned by the caller’s partition.⌋(SRS_Rte_00210)
[SWS_Rte_02753] ⌈When a SW-C in an untrusted partition passes an ArgumentDataPrototype or VariableDataPrototype, as a reference type to a SW-C in a trusted partition (DATA_REFERENCE as an IN parameter), the RTE shall only check that the caller’s partition owns the start address of the referenced memory.⌋(SRS_Rte_00210) Note to [SWS_Rte_02753]: The RTE only checks whether the start address referenced directly by the DataPrototypes belongs to the calling partition. Because the RTE is not aware of the semantic of the pointed reference, it cannot check if the referenced object is completely contained in the calling partition (e.g. the RTE does not know the size and does not know if the referenced object also contains references to other objects). The BSW is responsible to make sure that the referenced memory object does not cross memory section boundaries. The OS API CheckTaskMemoryAccess can be used to fulfill [SWS_Rte_02752] and
[SWS_Rte_02753].
